learning.title: Call the installed binary when a mise-wrapped CLI hangs with no output
learning.trigger: A CLI such as rig or gh exits 124 under timeout with zero bytes on stdout and stderr, even for --version or --help, while git against the same remote works.
learning.rule: Check what the shim is before debugging the tool. /home/marktripoli/.local/bin/rig runs "mise exec node@22.22.0 -- rig" and /home/marktripoli/.local/bin/gh runs "mise use -g --quiet gh" first; both resolve versions over the network on every call, so a network or provider outage makes every invocation hang before the tool starts. Call the installed binary directly instead: ~/.local/share/mise/installs/node/22.22.0/bin/rig and ~/.local/share/mise/installs/gh/latest/gh_2.100.0_linux_amd64/bin/gh (verify the path with ls of the installs dir). A whole seat can look wedged for hours this way while the agent's own reasoning is fine; the give-away is that even --version hangs.

verification.requirement: Prove it with exit codes, not impressions: the wrapper path times out (124, empty output) and the direct binary prints a version and exits 0 in the same shell. Record the working absolute path in the handover so the next occupant does not rediscover it.
